attempts.reason:
Strong PR — the three-rule design (open reloads on a tip change, a durable verb commits→loads→events→wakes,
a live verb touches only the index) is right, the conformance suite taking the composed driver is the proof
that mattered, and finding the verb gap with a CLI smoke rather than shipping it unnoticed is exactly the
honesty this needs. The gap itself is accepted as you scoped it: routing the verbs is #304's, and half-routing
would be worse than neither.

A high-effort review found 15 defects. CI is green, 1286 tests pass — this is an incomplete PR, not a broken
one. But read the headline first, because six of these share one shape and three of them lose data.

**The shape: the local path is checked *after* the GitHub path has already run, and the answer is reported as
complete either way.**

- `gc.sweep` branches on `storeKind` for two sweeps — after opening with an unconditional GitHub
  `fetchBoard` (gc.js:307). On a genuinely local board it throws before `stats.store` is ever read, so the
  skip message you wrote can only be seen by a board that is *also* on GitHub.
- `sync()` decides whether to fetch by calling `this.board()` (local.js:304), which throws when there is no
  branch — so the `skipped: 'no-branch'` answer at line 342 is unreachable code.
- The import reads blockers with the GitHub default and never asks `blockersKnown()`.
- `resolveStore` never consults `localBoardExists` while `storeKind` documents it as rule 2.

Every one of these is silent. Fix the shape, not only the six instances.

## Must fix — the migration loses data, and it is the one operation nobody re-runs

1. **`hkb init --import` erases the dependency graph of most cards** (local.js:572). `listTasks({states:['OPEN']})`
   takes `blockers: true`, whose `wanted` predicate is `t.status === 'todo' || t.status === 'blocked'`. On a repo
   without the GraphQL blocked-by capability, every card in `triage`/`ready`/`running`/`review` skips
   `fillBlockedByRest`, so `blockedBy` is `[]`, and `cardRecord` writes `blocked_by: []` to the branch. The DAG
   is gone. `src/model.js` has `blockersKnown()` *precisely* to tell "not looked up" from "nothing blocks it",
   and `cardRecord` ignores it. Pass `{states:['OPEN'], blockers:'all'}`, and make `cardRecord` refuse rather
   than write `[]` when blockers are unknown.

2. **A card whose blocker was not imported is permanently blocked, silently** (local.js:585). #40 is open and
   blocked by #12, closed 200 days ago (outside the window) or not on this board. `cardRecord(#40)` keeps
   `blocked_by: [12]`; on read `toTask` resolves the unknown id to `{number: 12, state: 'OPEN'}`, so
   `blockerDone()` is false forever and `computeReady()` never returns true. #40 can never be dispatched on the
   migrated board, with nothing in the summary saying a blocker was dropped. Either import the blocker
   regardless of the window, or drop the edge and **say so in the import summary** — never silently keep an
   edge that cannot resolve.

3. **`listClosedRecent({first: 100})` is one unpaginated page** (local.js:573), and `fetchClosedRecent`'s own
   comment says "One query, no paging". A board with 300 cards closed in the window imports the 100 most
   recently updated and prints `100 closed in the last 90 day(s)`, which reads as the whole window. `next_id`
   is computed from the truncated set. Paginate, or make the cap explicit in the summary and in the refusal.

   1–3 compound: 3 drops cards, 2 turns each dropped card into a permanent block on whatever depended on it,
   and 1 removes the edges that would have made it visible. A migrated board can look fine and never dispatch.

## Must fix — the rest

4. **A track-only tick never syncs and never re-stamps** (dispatch.js:1204). `DURABLE_TICK_KEYS` omits `tracks`
   and `spawn_failed`, but a successful track-root dispatch does `saveRun` and `setStatus(t,'running')` — both
   durable — and reports only into `summary.tracks`. So on a board driven by track dispatch the branch is never
   pushed and the stamp goes stale; after `HOST_LIVE_MS` another host's `--take-over` sees
   `liveDispatcher() === null` and takes a board that is actively ticking. That is the two-writers case §6.2
   exists to prevent, reached from the inside.

5. **`hkb sync` refuses on exactly the checkout it exists for** (local.js:304) — and this one breaks a stated
   product requirement, not just an edge. `sync()` opens with `this.board()`, which throws `there is no
   kb-board branch` when the branch is not local yet. A `--single-branch` clone, or one taken before the branch
   was pushed, therefore cannot fetch it, and `hkb init` there creates a *second, empty* board instead of
   adopting the remote's. The requirement this is for, in the operator's own words: **"if a friend clones the
   repo, I want them to have the board as well."** Read the ref state first, fetch, and only then read the
   board.

6. **`sync.push: false` disables fetch and fast-forward too, and `--no-push` bypasses the switch entirely**
   (local.js:304). The guard is `settings.push === false && push`, checked before the fetch. So a host that opted
   out of pushing can never pull a co-worker's commits — and `hkb sync --no-push` sets `push` false, the `&& push`
   is false, the guard does not fire, and the more restrictive flag does strictly *more* work than the default.
   `hkb init`'s own message ("so kb-board is never pushed") describes push-only behaviour the code does not
   implement.

7. **`markDispatcher()` bypasses `_durable`** (local.js:280): it commits with a raw `git.setBoard()` and never
   reloads the index, so from the first stamp `index.tip() !== git.tip()` and `hkb doctor` prints a *permanent*
   index warning on a healthy board — for as long as the board is up. It also puts a `hkb: board settings`
   commit on `git log kb-board` every 5 minutes, against the module's own rule that the log is a history of
   decisions. (Your own residual note called the commit rate a cost; the doctor warning makes it a bug.)

8. **`OFFLINE` does not match `ETIMEDOUT`** (local.js:42). `runGit` defaults to a 30 s timeout; on timeout
   `spawnSync` sets `res.error` and the output carries `spawnSync git ETIMEDOUT`, which matches none of
   `connection timed out` / `operation timed out` / `could not resolve host`. `status` is `null`, so `!== 0` is
   true and `hkb sync` throws exit 2 pointing at a remote that is fine — on precisely the "laptop that spends
   its day on and off a network" your doc comment says the tolerance is for.

9. **`resolveStore` and `storeKind` disagree, and `init` writes the wrong answer back** (init.js:672).
   `storeKind` rule 2 says a repository with a `kb-board` branch *is* local — "what makes a `git clone` of a
   local board work with no config at all". `resolveStore` never calls `localBoardExists`. So in a checkout with
   a live branch full of cards but a `board.json` without the key, `hkb init` answers `github`, writes
   `cfg.store = 'github'`, and permanently detaches the board from its branch. The two JSDoc blocks state the
   contradiction in words. One function decides, and the other calls it.

10. **`gc` on a genuinely local board fails before it reaches the store** (gc.js:307) — above.

11. **`mountFor` keeps the first of two entries sharing a mount point** (local.js:658); `>` should be `>=`,
    because the effective filesystem is the last one mounted there. An overlay or bind remounted over `/` reads
    as the underlying `ext4` — and a network filesystem remounted over a local path is exactly what the probe
    exists to catch.

12. **The beat-chain cleanup is unguarded** (local.js:620) while the lock-ref loop directly above it is wrapped.
    `dropBeatChain` shells out; one locked ref throws out of `importGithubBoard` *after* both commits and the
    index load succeeded, `setUpLocalBoard` has no catch either, and `hkb init --import` exits non-zero on a
    board that fully migrated — leaving the human unable to tell whether to re-run, which "idempotent by
    refusal" will then reject.

## Also fix — cost, and you flagged two of these yourself

13. **`syncPass` blocks the dispatcher's event loop for up to 60 s** (dispatch.js:1222): `markDispatcher()` and
    `syncAfterTick()` are synchronous and reach the network through `spawnSync`, twice, at 30 s each. While they
    run, `watchChild`'s exit handlers cannot fire, the sleeper cannot be woken, and `hkb down`'s SIGTERM is not
    handled. Value 3 is performance and the loop is the thing that must stay responsive.
14. **`assertOwningHost` decodes the whole board tree per write verb, then the verb's own store decodes it
    again** (cli.js:451 → local.js:449): `openGitTier` → `tip()` → `readTree()`, a full `ls-tree -r` plus
    `cat-file --batch`, to read one string. Two whole-board decodes per `hkb create` on a 500-card board, nothing
    memoized across them. Separately `storeKind` shells out two `git rev-parse` on every `WRITES_BOARD` command,
    every `syncPass` (before the cheap `DURABLE_TICK_KEYS` test, which should come first) and every `gc.sweep`,
    for GitHub boards that gain nothing.
15. **`_durable` rebuilds the entire index per verb** (local.js:123): two extra `rev-parse` to re-derive
    "changed", then `readTree()`'s `structuredClone` of every card and run, then `DELETE`+re-`INSERT` of the whole
    board. `GitTier.commit()` already returns `{changed, tip}` and has already re-parsed the landed tree into
    `_snap`. A tick touching twenty cards pays twenty full-board clones and twenty full rebuilds — the same
    hazard git.js's own comment warns about.

## Done when

- [ ] Every item fixed, or one line on the card arguing why not — your item-15 pushback last card was right and
      that is the bar.
- [ ] A test for 1–9 and 11–12. For 1 and 2 the test must assert the *summary* reports what was dropped.
- [ ] The shape sweep: for each fix, where else does a local answer get decided after the GitHub path ran, or
      get truncated and reported as complete?
- [ ] Two of your own residual notes are on this list (the 5-minute commit, the 100-card cap). Where a residual
      note names a real defect, fix it rather than recording it.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.

   triage" path is skipped because `store !== 'github'`. README line 35 still promises this command
   "pulls your existing open issues onto the board as triage". Two different operations now share one
   flag: migrating an existing kb board onto the local store, and adopting a repo's issues onto a new
   board. Give them separate names, or dispatch on whether a kb board exists — and make the log say
   which one ran.

2. **`cfg.store = store` pins `"github"` on every existing board that re-runs init** (init.js:971), after
   which the documented migration can never run: `hkb init --import` reads the pinned value, never calls
   `setUpLocalBoard`, and silently does the old adopt loop instead. Only `--store local --import` works,
   which the README does not say. Write the key when the human chose it, not when it was inferred — or
   have `--import` mean "migrate" regardless of the pin.

3. **`closedFilled` is always false** (local.js:720) — above. Needs a real path through for a repo without
   `blockedByGql`: import closed cards with their blockers marked unknown and report them, or skip the
   closed half and say so, but do not dead-end the migration.

4. **Liveness expires on an idle dispatcher** (dispatch.js:1231) — above. `markDispatcher()` belongs

5. **Clock skew makes the take-over guard fail open** (local.js:479). `liveDispatcher` returns null when
   `age < 0`, so a stamp 30 seconds in the future — ordinary skew between two hosts, or one RTC that
   drifted — reads as *no live dispatcher* and `--take-over` proceeds while A's loop is writing. Fail
   closed: a future stamp is a live dispatcher, not an absent one.

6. **`wake()` has never worked, and starts a debugger instead** (local.js:142). `_durable` ends every write
   with `index.wake()` → SIGUSR1, and **nothing in `src/` installs a SIGUSR1 handler** — the only match is
   `sqlite.js` sending it. Node's default action for SIGUSR1 is to start the inspector, so a verb writing a
   local board while `hkb dispatch --loop` is up opens `Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/…` on the
   dispatcher rather than waking it. There is also no self-pid guard, so once the dispatcher writes through
   the store (track C) it signals itself. Either install the handler in the loop and make it interrupt the
   sleeper, or drop the wake and say the tick interval is the latency.

7. **`hkb up --status` is refused on a non-owning host** (cli.js:451). `up` is in `WRITES_BOARD`, so a
   teammate who cloned a board owned by another host cannot ask what is running — a command documented as
   "pid files and liveness, no board read and no network". `hkb up --serve` is refused too, though `hkb
   serve` alone is deliberately allowed. Guard the verb that writes, not the noun.

8. **`sweepAgentWorktrees` is inert on a local board and says nothing** (gc.js:328). `GitTier.toTask`
   hardcodes `prs: []`, so `prByBranch` is always null and every `agent-*` worktree is skipped. `hkb gc
   --yes` reports 0 removed and the checkouts accumulate forever — while the two sweeps directly below it
   *do* announce that they were skipped for this store. Either resolve the PR through the forge or say the
   sweep is inert here.

9. **`sweepTrackBranches` still runs on a local board** (gc.js:331) — a `gh api` request per gc and per
   `gc_every_ticks` tick for an answer that is structurally always empty, plus a noisy "skipped" line from

10. **`checkPathOverlapGuard` now lives inside `githubChecks`** (doctor.js:1561) though it reads only
    `ctx.cfg`. A stale `repo` or a logged-out `gh` throws at the labels call, the catch emits one
    `bad('github', …)` and returns — so a malformed `dispatch.guards.path_overlap` is never reported, on a
    check that needs no network at all. That split exists precisely so a GitHub failure cannot swallow
    local checks.

11. **`LocalStore.assertOwner()` has no production caller** (local.js:266) — `git grep` finds only its
    definition and `test/store-local.test.js:142`. So the PR's "three layers" of the owning-host guard is
    two, and the result comment says otherwise. Worse, `owner()` goes through `git.board()`, which throws
    on a branchless board where the module-level `assertLocalOwner` deliberately returns null — so wiring
    it in later would refuse a board the other two layers pass. Wire it or delete it, and correct the
    claim.

12. **`addNote` files a result the tier will not** (local.js:229) — it classifies on
    `startsWith(RESULT_MARKER)` alone while `GitTier.addNote` also requires `parseResultComment` to
    succeed. A malformed result body is stored as a *note* and announced as a `result` event, so `hkb watch
    --kinds result` and serve's stream report a handoff `latestResult(n)` will never return. This is the
    same divergence shape as the `listNotes` finding on #315 — two code paths deciding "is this a result"
    with different rules. One predicate, used by both.

13. **The beat-chain message names refs that do not exist** (local.js:809): it says `refs/kb/beats/`, while
    `listBeatChains`/`dropBeatChain` read and write `refs/kb/locks/`. The operator following that advice
    finds nothing.

14. **`storeKind` caches only the `local` answer** (index.js:59), so every board predating the key — this
    repo's included — re-spawns two `git rev-parse` per write verb, per `gc.sweep` and per `syncPass`, to

    branch underfoot, but `init` already calls `forgetStore(ctx)` for exactly that, so the negative can be
    cached and invalidated the same way.

1. **`hkb init --import` on *this* repo kills running workers and flips the tracked board.json**
   (init.js:978). `.kanban/board.json` here is tracked and has no `store` key, so `resolveStore` says
   `github`; the new override then routes `--import` to `setUpLocalBoard` → `importGithubBoard` →
   `dropGithubLeftovers`, which calls `release(ctx, n, k)` for **every** `refs/kb/locks/*` on the remote.

   drive GitHub. The command that does this is the one the README has documented for months. It must
   refuse when the board has live locks, refuse (or prompt) when board.json is tracked, and never delete a
   lock it did not verify is dead.

2. **`dropGithubLeftovers` is repo-wide, not board-scoped** (local.js:946). `refs/kb/locks/<n>/<k>` has no
   board segment, and `listLocks(ctx)` / `listBeatChains(root)` enumerate the namespace, so migrating board
   `alpha` deletes board `beta`'s live locks and beta's workers lose their claims. Scope the sweep to the
   cards actually migrated, at minimum.

3. **`hkb dispatch --loop N --dry-run` skips the owner guard and then writes anyway** (cli.js:100).
   `invocationWritesBoard` treats any `dispatch` carrying `--dry-run` as a read, so `assertOwningHost` is

   `dryRun` at all**. So on a clone of someone else's board the flag that promises not to write both
   removes the guard and runs a real claiming, spawning, stamping loop. Either thread `dryRun` into
   `loop()` or treat `--loop` as a write regardless of `--dry-run`; the flag combination must not be the
   one that gets through.

5. **Every command on every board now loads `node:sqlite`** (store/index.js:19). `store/index.js` and

7. **`markDispatcher` does a full `_reindex()`** (local.js:329) — above.

9. **`syncPass` builds and tears down a whole `LocalStore` every tick** (dispatch.js:1237) — a fresh

    raised flag renders as "cleared". Give each op its own kind, or carry the fields `describeEvent` reads.

    else that creates the branch mid-process invalidates the same way init does" — `sync()` does not call
    `forgetStore`. Make the claim true.

13. **`serve` is out of `WRITES_BOARD` on the ground that serving a clone read-only is fine**
    (cli.js:97) — but serve's drag-and-drop runs the same mutating verbs, as its own HELP line says. A
    non-owning host gets a writable UI whose every drag dies inside the tier with a raw exit-2. Refuse at

1. **`hkb init --import` erases the dependency graph of most cards** (local.js:572). `listTasks({states:['OPEN']})`

   without the GraphQL blocked-by capability, every card in `triage`/`ready`/`running`/`review` skips
   `fillBlockedByRest`, so `blockedBy` is `[]`, and `cardRecord` writes `blocked_by: []` to the branch. The DAG
   is gone. `src/model.js` has `blockersKnown()` *precisely* to tell "not looked up" from "nothing blocks it",
   and `cardRecord` ignores it. Pass `{states:['OPEN'], blockers:'all'}`, and make `cardRecord` refuse rather
   than write `[]` when blockers are unknown.

2. **A card whose blocker was not imported is permanently blocked, silently** (local.js:585). #40 is open and
   blocked by #12, closed 200 days ago (outside the window) or not on this board. `cardRecord(#40)` keeps

1. A LIVE CLAIM STOPS THE MIGRATION BEFORE THE FIRST COMMIT. `liveLocks(ctx, {keep})` reads each lock ref's last beat (`lockBeatAt`) and a beat inside `LOCK_LIVE_S` (30 min) means a worker is holding that card; the refusal names the cards and `hkb init --import --force`, which migrates anyway and logs what it costs. A lock LISTING that fails is logged rather than read as 'no locks' — that answer is the one that would justify deleting them, and the deletion half is guarded the same way, so nothing is lost either way. Test asserts the throw, `git.tip() === null` (not one commit landed) and that `release` was never called, then that `--force` gets through and says LOCK_LOST.

2. THE SWEEP IS SCOPED, AND VERIFIES EACH REF DEAD. `refs/kb/locks/<n>/<k>` carries no board segment, so `listLocks(ctx)` enumerates the whole repository: migrating board alpha deleted beta's live locks. `dropGithubLeftovers` now takes `keep` (the ids actually migrated) for both the locks and the beat chains, re-checks `lockIsLive` per ref, and reports `locks_kept` / `locks_foreign` / `chains_foreign` in the summary and the log.

3. THE TRACKED board.json IS NOT FLIPPED. `boardFileTracked(root)` (new, exported, tested) — `hkb init --import` refuses to write `"store": "local"` into a git-tracked `.kanban/board.json` without `--force`, because that key is every collaborator's next pull. And the key is written AFTER the migration lands (`writeStoreKey()` moved below `setUpLocalBoard`), so a refusal leaves the board exactly where it was rather than pointing every verb at an empty branch. The pin *condition* is unchanged — only its timing.

THE OTHER TWO GUARD HOLES:

4. `hkb dispatch --loop --dry-run` is a write. `invocationWritesBoard` exempts a dry run only when there is no `--loop` (a loop stamps and pushes, which no per-tick flag gates), AND `dryRun` is now threaded into `loop()` → `tick()` — it was dropped outright, so the pair removed the guard and then ran a real claiming, spawning, stamping loop. `syncPass` is skipped on a dry run for the same reason.

5. `hkb serve` joins `WRITES_BOARD`. The page's drag-and-drop runs the same mutating verbs, so a non-owning host got a writable UI whose every drag died inside the tier with a raw exit 2. `src/serve.js` is out of this card's scope and has no read-only mode, so the honest fix is refusing at start-up and naming the read verbs (`hkb list/show/graph/watch`); README and the wiki now say that instead of promising a read-only web board.

· CLOCKS (grep: every `Date.parse`/`getTime()` in local.js). The rule is NOT 'clamp every clock' — it is 'answer skew with the live board'. A LIVENESS GUARD clamps a future timestamp and refuses: `liveDispatcher` (already did), `lockIsLive` (new, clamped). A THROTTLE must NOT clamp: `markDispatcher` and `syncAfterTick` now skip the throttle on a negative delta, because a timestamp after `now` is not freshness, it is a value to rewrite. Clamping `markDispatcher` — which is what the review's wording literally asked for — would have KEPT the bug: `Math.max(0, …)` is still `< HOST_LIVE_MS/3`, so stamping would still have stopped for twenty minutes after a backwards NTP step. ITEM 1 IS A DECISION, AND THE ANSWER IS YES: rule 2 is removed. `storeKind` now reads `"store"` in `.kanban/board.json` and nothing else; an absent key is `github`. The reviewer's case is the whole argument — a rule that reads the store off a *ref* is reachable by `git fetch`, and the resulting half-migrated state (local store, GitHub cards) produced a different destructive interaction in each of three rounds: an `--import` that deleted live workers' lock refs, a `gc.sweep` that read `[]` and destroyed worker worktrees with uncommitted work in them, and one host's push refusing every collaborator's writes on a board of issues they own. What rule 2 bought — "a clone needs no configuration" — is bought better by the key: `.kanban/board.json` is a *tracked* file, so the key rides in with the clone, and that does not depend on which refs a particular clone happens to carry (`--single-branch`, a stale fetch, a mirror). A checkout that has the branch but not the key is told so in words by `hkb init` and `hkb doctor` — a message, never a behaviour. This collapsed items 2 and 3 and deleted item 12 outright (`openStore(ctx, {kind})` had no caller; there is no cache to invalidate either, so `forgetStore` now only drops the memoized git tiers).

THE OTHER TWO THAT COULD DESTROY WORK:
1. `gc.sweep` sweeps NOTHING when the board comes back with no cards — worktrees, branches, agent worktrees, track branches, comments and beat chains all gated, `empty_board` in the stats, and a line saying why. A board that returned nothing is a board that could not be read, not one where every card is done, and the dispatcher runs this with `yes: true` every `gc_every_ticks`. THE RULE SWEEP found the same shape twice more, in the tick: `reapDecision(j, null)` stops a background agent and sweeps its checkout, and the orphan lock sweep releases a lock whose card is missing (a worker whose ref disappears exits LOCK_LOST). Those are deliberately NOT gated, and the reason is written where they are: `fetchBoard` reads the *open* board, so "no cards" is an ordinary correct state — a board whose last card just closed — and gating it would stop reaping exactly the agent that closing card left behind. I staged the guard, watched `test/reap.test.js` fail on precisely that case, and took it out. What makes absence safe there is that `fetchBoard` throws rather than answering `[]`, and that no inference can now point a tick at a store the cards are not on.
2. The loop's teardown is a `finally` and takes all four listeners (SIGUSR1, SIGINT, SIGTERM) plus `dropLock()`. SIGINT/SIGTERM were never removed at all — found by asking what the invariant was rather than patching the one listener named.

THE CLOCK, WHICH IS ONE FUNCTION NOW. `throttled(now, last, window)` is exported from `src/store/local.js` and used by `markDispatcher` and `syncAfterTick`: fresh means inside the window ON EITHER SIDE of now. A backward NTP step is throttled, never "due", so the every-tick stamp-and-push is gone and so is the flake. Nothing is lost by holding off on a future stamp — every *reader* of it (`liveDispatcher`, `lockIsLive`, both clamped) already treats it as live, which is the sentence that makes the two families agree instead of contradicting. A stamp further ahead than the window is not skew but a broken record, so it is rewritten once and throttles normally after. `test/store-local.test.js` ran 20 times: 20/20 green, and the test injects the backward step rather than relying on timing.

THE REST: doctor's forge half runs each probe under its own `step(name, …)`, so one 404 costs one line instead of every check after it (the board-consuming checks already say "could not read the board" under their own names, which is what makes a skipped check distinguishable from a passing one); the import's "branch already exists" refusal computes the index path with `indexFileIn` instead of opening the database it tells you to delete; `root()` is a method on both drivers and is on `STORE_METHODS`, so the shape check can catch the next such disagreement; a mixed label batch keeps every label in the payload (kind `needs-human` only when the flag is the whole write); the adoption ceiling reads the page above the last full one before claiming anything was left off, and the migration's closed-card cap says "may be more" since it has no page to ask; `sync()` reads its two refs once instead of on every return path; `WRITES_BOARD`'s comment agrees with `WRITES_BOARD`; and `RESULT_MARKER` is no longer imported unused (a sweep for that pattern across all ten touched files found nothing else).

STATIC IMPORTS: `openStore` and `assertOwningHost` are async and reach `local.js` through `await import`, as does `checkLocalStore`, so a GitHub board never loads `node:sqlite` — two layers now, since `sqlite.js` also resolves the builtin lazily. That rippled: `openStore` callers (`gc.sweep`, the conformance suite, `test/store-local.test.js`) await it.
